newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cert coffee stocks slip to new 12-year low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cert coffee stocks slip to new 12-year low.

text.p: U.S. certified coffee stocks fell by 945 60-kg bags in the week ended October 4, to set a new 12-year low of 30,724 bags, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Monday.
The draw occurred solely in the exchange's Miami warehouse, where stocks dropped to 1,269 bags, a decline of more than four percent on the week.
The drawdown was well within expectations, although some traders said Monday's afternoon rally may have been fueled by rumours of a steeper decline.
More importantly, traders said, was the absence of coffee pending certification again this week.
"That is better news for the market than the drop in stocks," said one.

But other traders said the lack of coffee awaiting exchange approval was not surprising, since producers were receiving hefty premiums selling directly to roasters and were unlikely to sell to the CSCE for prices listed on the board.

Last week, the exchange-certified stockpile shrank to its lowest level in more than a decade, falling more than 10,000 bags to 31,669 bags. The steep downturn revived near-term supply concerns and sparked five consecutive higher closes on the futures market.
Since last Monday, the benchmark December contract gained 9.75 cents, or more than nine percent.
Worries about tight spot supplies also buoyed the nearby December/March switch, which balloned to 6.50 cents by the close Monday, up from 3.45 cents a week ago.
Spot December coffee rose 2.90 cents per lb on Monday, to finish at 112.70 cents, while March ended 2.10 cents higher, at 106.25 cents.
